summary: Frontend-only validation of iter106ap avatar placeholder-filter + expo-image object-form + onError-fallback fix. Verified via (a) 19-case Node unit test of resolveAvatarUrl inlined from src/utils/avatar.ts, (b) source-tree inspection of TrainerAvatar.tsx / UserAvatar.tsx / admin/UsersTab.tsx, (c) live backend curl (admin/users list, admin/users/{id}, trainer-profiles/{id}, auth/login) against the deployed ingress. Playwright UI validation skipped per explicit review-request instruction (deployed web preview serves stale /dist; iOS bundle out of scope). FOUND ONE CRITICAL BUG in the fix itself — the placeholder regex fails to match the primary case it claims to filter — plus one duplication concern and one edge case.

ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL: placeholder regex `/(^|\.)example\.com\b/i` FAILS to match `https://example.com/foo.jpg`. The character preceding `example.com` in a bare-domain URL is `/` (from the `://`), which is neither start-of-string nor `.`. Verified by 19-case unit test: `https://example.com/foo.png` returns the URL unchanged (should be null); only subdomain forms like `https://cdn.example.com/x.png` are filtered. Live data scan (curl /api/admin/users?limit=500 with admin creds) confirms 25 users in production carry `https://example.com/trainer-photo.jpg` or `https://example.com/trainee-photo.jpg` in avatarUrl / profilePhoto (all the TEST_ITER27_*_pop_trainer / pop_trainee accounts + the population-test trainee explicitly named in the review request). These will NOT be short-circuited to initials as the fix intends — the intended `example.com` hard-drop is a no-op for the primary URL form. At runtime the onError fallback should still eventually show initials because example.com returns 404 for these paths, but (a) that reintroduces the exact flash-of-blank-circle + wasted-network-round-trip UX the fix was written to eliminate, and (b) it relies on expo-image reliably firing onError on iOS which is the exact quirk cited as motivation for the fix. Fix: replace regex with `/(?:^|[./:])example\.com\b/i` (adds `/` and `:` to the pre-boundary class) OR — better — use `new URL(trimmed).hostname === 'example.com' || .endsWith('.example.com')` guarded by try/catch for non-URL inputs. Apply in BOTH avatar.ts AND TrainerAvatar.tsx (both have the same buggy check).

DRY violation — the placeholder detection `/(^|\.)example\.com\b/i.test(cleaned) || cleaned.endsWith('/some-photo.png')` is duplicated verbatim from src/utils/avatar.ts lines 51-52. Any fix to the regex has to land in two files or one will drift. Recommend exporting `isPlaceholderAvatarUrl(url: string): boolean` from utils/avatar.ts and calling it from both.

`trimmed.endsWith('/some-photo.png')` is fragile — a URL like `/api/files/some-photo.png?v=2` or `/api/files/some-photo.png#foo` would slip through. No live-data hits today (0/444 users have this URL currently — the test_trainer that historically carried it now has a real data-URI), so LOW priority, but recommend `/\/some-photo\.png(\?|#|$)/i.test(trimmed)` for correctness.

This is the App-Store-visible symptom the fix was meant to solve.

critical_code_review_comments: TrainerAvatar.tsx duplicates the placeholder-detection regex from avatar.ts — this is a maintenance trap; both files must be edited in lockstep for any placeholder-list change. Extract into a shared helper.

resolveAvatarUrl currently short-circuits at the first non-null field; when that field is a placeholder it returns null and does NOT try the next field (profilePhoto/photoUrl/etc.). Live data confirms this is the correct behaviour for the 3 pop_trainee accounts that have example.com in BOTH profilePhoto AND avatarUrl, but a scenario where avatarUrl is example.com and profilePhoto is a valid data-URI would incorrectly go to initials. The unit-test matrix flags this — decide whether to keep the current behaviour or fall through to the next field after placeholder rejection.
TrainerAvatar re-runs the same placeholder check that resolveAvatarUrl already ran — belt-and-suspenders is fine, but only if the two implementations stay in sync (see DRY comment).

rca_of_the_issue: The iter106ap fix intended to hard-drop example.com and /some-photo.png placeholder URLs so blank-circle avatars would fall through to the colored-initials block. The example.com regex `(^|\.)example\.com\b` was written to match either bare 'example.com...' or 'sub.example.com...' — but URLs are almost always of the form `https://example.com/...` in which the character *immediately preceding* `example.com` is `/`, not `.` and not start-of-string. Hence the primary case is silently unmatched. Live-data scan proved 25 users out of 444 still have this exact pattern. Runtime effect is partly masked by TrainerAvatar's onError→setImgFailed fallback (introduced in the same fix), but only if expo-image reliably fires onError on iOS — the exact quirk the review request cites as motivation. Reproduction: `resolveAvatarUrl({avatarUrl:'https://example.com/trainer-photo.jpg'})` returns the URL unchanged; expected `null`. Mitigation: expand regex to `/(?:^|[./:])example\.com\b/i` (adds `/` and `:` to the char-class before the host) — or, more robust, `try { const h = new URL(trimmed).hostname; if (h === 'example.com' || h.endsWith('.example.com')) return null; } catch {}`. Apply the identical change in TrainerAvatar.tsx line 92.
